question: Why are my floor tiles popping up or sounding hollow?
title: Why Floor Tiles Pop Up or Sound Hollow
h1: Why Is a Tile Popping Up or Sounding Hollow When You Walk On It?
description: Hollow tile is almost always missing movement joints plus a weak bond; TCNA EJ171 requires joints every 20-25 ft indoors, 8-12 ft in sun or moisture.
capsule: Hollow or popping tile is almost always caused by missing movement joints combined with a weak mortar bond, not one single defect. TCNA's EJ171 standard calls for movement joints every 20-25 feet indoors, but every 8-12 feet where tile sits in direct sun or gets wet - common on Florida lanais and pool baths.

sections.h2: What's actually happening under a hollow-sounding tile
sections.html:
Tap a tile and get a dead, hollow knock instead of a solid one, and the tile has lost its bond to the substrate underneath. Per CTaSC, a tile-industry testing lab, this is almost never one clean cause - it's usually compounding defects stacking up: a thin or inconsistent mortar bed, a dusty or sealed slab the thinset never gripped, and no room anywhere in the field for the tile to expand and contract. Any one of those alone might not tent a floor. Together, they will.

Once a tile has lost bond, walking on it flexes that hollow spot, and the grout line next to it takes the stress. That's when you start seeing a tile actually lift at the edge or a grout joint crack in a straight line across the room. This is different from a tile that's simply chipped or cracked from impact - a hollow sound points to a bond failure under the surface, not just surface damage, which is why it's worth an inspection rather than a quick grout touch-up.

sections.h2: Do tile floors need expansion joints?
sections.html:
Yes. Every tile installation needs somewhere to move as the slab and the tile itself expand and contract with temperature - TCNA's own FAQ is blunt about it. In a small bathroom, the gap hidden under the baseboard around the room's perimeter is usually enough room. In a larger great room or an open kitchen-to-lanai layout, that perimeter gap alone isn't enough - the field needs visible movement joints per TCNA EJ171, typically filled with a flexible sealant instead of grout.

EJ171 sets the spacing: every 20-25 ft in each direction for interior tile away from sunlight and moisture, tightening to every 8-12 ft wherever the tile gets direct sun or gets wet - and that includes most of Florida's covered lanais, pool decks and sunrooms.

sections.h2: Where this shows up most in Sarasota and Manatee County homes
sections.html: We see it most on older jobs - tile set in the 1990s and 2000s before movement-joint spacing was as widely followed - and on additions where an indoor tile field runs straight through a sliding door onto a covered lanai with no joint at the transition. A 30-ft-wide great room with no interior movement joint is a textbook EJ171 violation, and it's common in homes built before the standard was routinely enforced by installers. Homes that have gone through a hurricane season with a leaking window or door threshold are also more prone to hollow tile near that opening, since repeated wetting and drying of the mortar bed underneath weakens the bond faster than normal wear.

LocationRequired movement joint spacing (TCNA EJ171)
Interior tile, no direct sun or moistureEvery 20-25 ft, each direction
Interior tile in direct sunlight or wet areasEvery 8-12 ft, each direction
Outdoor tile (lanai, pool deck)Every 8-12 ft, each direction

A single hollow tile can sometimes be re-bonded by injecting epoxy underneath it, but once hollow spots run in a pattern along a straight line, that's a sign the whole field is missing joints, and patching one tile won't fix the next one. At that point we're usually pulling the affected section with tile removal and resetting it as part of a tile installation with correct movement joints and a full mortar bed, which typically runs $2.50-$4.50 per sq ft for the removal and chip-out before the new tile goes in. Smaller, isolated spots are often handled through our floor repair service instead of a full re-tile. Either way, ask for the diagnostic visit fee - $185, credited toward the repair - so you know the cost before work starts, and start that process with a free estimate.

faqs.q: Can I just replace the one hollow tile?
faqs.a: Sometimes, if it's an isolated spot and the rest of the field sounds solid. If several tiles in a row sound hollow, the underlying cause is usually missing movement joints across the whole field, and one tile fixed won't stop the next one from failing.

faqs.q: Does grout cracking always mean the tile underneath is hollow?
faqs.a: Not always, but a straight-line crack running across multiple tiles is a common sign the field has no movement joint at that point and the tile and substrate are fighting each other.

faqs.q: Is hollow tile dangerous to walk on?
faqs.a: A hollow tile can crack or shift underfoot, and a loose piece is a trip hazard. It won't fix itself, and it tends to spread to neighboring tiles over time.
